rows.subject: Local archive binary classification theorem
rows.exact_statement: A whole-document public/private binary filing system cannot classify a mixed document that must release one part and withhold another; a richer label space can.
rows.proposition: For parts p,q with obligations release(p)=true and release(q)=false, no constant whole-document binary release function satisfies both; a part-level function does.
rows.falsifier: A binary whole-document label whose semantics releases p and withholds q.
rows.next_action: Use theorem as first local OC proof surface.

rows.subject: Overbroad central-principle universal reading
rows.exact_statement: Every contradiction, merely by being a contradiction, necessarily produces a new dimension or collapse.
rows.proposition: There exists a conflict resolved by already available descriptive structure; therefore no event-level new axis and no collapse are necessary.
rows.falsifier: Show that the existing-redaction archive still creates a new axis or collapses despite the already adequate operator.
rows.next_action: Keep counterproof as boundary against universal-law wording.

rows.subject: Bounded central schema
rows.exact_statement: When a description encounters an incompatibility it cannot represent within its present continuum, the next viable outcome is often either enrichment or collapse.
rows.proposition: Under explicit trigger assumptions, prove/refute that no same-description repair implies either conservative extension suffices or organization predicate fails.
rows.falsifier: A case satisfying trigger assumptions where neither extension nor organization failure occurs.
rows.next_action: Use only as bounded formal schema; continue primitive non-circularity audit.

rows.subject: Primitive package adequacy
rows.exact_statement: OC primitives include description, system, state, axis, continuum, boundary, operator, constraint, contradiction, resolution, collapse, and dimension birth.
rows.proposition: Prove/refute that the primitive package is non-circular and sufficient to state central-schema claims.
rows.falsifier: A primitive used in CP whose meaning depends on CP outcome, or a CP proof requiring an undefined primitive.
rows.next_action: Use only for bounded schema; domain adequacy still requires local evidence.

rows.subject: Operator catalogue and minimality
rows.exact_statement: The six OC operators Birth, Differentiate, Stabilize, Project, Kill, Repair form a sufficient/minimal source catalogue.
rows.proposition: Prove local independence/sufficiency under typed effects, or refute stronger minimality/uniqueness.
rows.falsifier: One operator definable from others under same effect signature, or a required transition not covered by catalogue.
rows.next_action: Strong global minimality is refuted; six names remain optional semantic vocabulary.

rows.subject: K-level distinctness and count
rows.exact_statement: K0-K12 are the OC hierarchy levels and may be presented as distinct/count-complete.
rows.proposition: Prove adjacent distinctness and count/exhaustiveness, or refute uniqueness/exhaustiveness.
rows.falsifier: Alternative partition with same admissible work, or lack of invariant for an adjacent level.
rows.next_action: Strong unique/exhaustive K-level count is refuted; adjacent invariant distinctness remains a separate bounded theorem family.

rows.subject: Law-like OC statements
rows.exact_statement: OC law-like statements can be promoted only when theorem, bounded schema, or empirically evidenced.
rows.proposition: For each recovered law-like sentence, prove theorem status or refute promoted law wording.
rows.falsifier: A promoted law statement without proof, source model, or falsifier.
rows.next_action: Unconditional law-promotion wording is refuted; only bounded theorem/schema wording survives.

rows.subject: Crown-stone consequences
rows.exact_statement: Crown-stone claims are established consequences of OC.
rows.proposition: Prove theorem-chain consequence for each crown-stone, or refute established-consequence wording.
rows.falsifier: A crown-stone not derivable from closed theorem chain.
rows.next_action: Established-consequence wording is refuted by failed strong dependencies.

rows.subject: Domain projection validation
rows.exact_statement: OC projections across domains are validated by the core theory.
rows.proposition: Prove local projection with variables/falsifier/evidence, or refute validation wording as overclaim.
rows.falsifier: A domain projection lacking local observables, operators, or falsifier.
rows.next_action: Core-only domain validation wording is refuted; local evidence remains required.
